background: Bank of Ireland Group is the holding company of Ireland's other dominant retail and business bank, funded by Irish deposits and lending on Irish and UK mortgages and to Irish companies, with a UK consumer finance arm.
synthesis: Rated A- on average across two of the three, both on a stable outlook, after one of the three withdrew its rating on 25 Mar 2026. Liquidity is the strength, with LCR of 193% and NSFR of 153% both in the top quarter of EU and Nordic banks, and leverage of 6.8% is above the peer median; CET1 of 14.9% is below the median and is the softer figure. Leverage has risen 0.5 points since 30 Jun 2024 while the other ratios have been broadly flat, on figures to 31 Mar 2026. Recent news is mostly good on earnings, and the newest flag, on 8 Oct 2026, reports losses on US leveraged finance loans contained with insurance deals.
